messages.text: I recorded this explanation in OBS today. Please turn the recordings in raw/ into one focused portrait educational short for YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, and TikTok. Use the screen and camera footage appropriately. Deliver one finished 1080 × 1920 video with readable captions positioned for the three platforms, timed caption files, and an editable project here for me to review. Don't post it to any social platform.

I’ll review the recordings, choose a self-contained takeaway, and build a portrait edit with cleaned voice, captions, and supporting graphics. I’m using the edit-video, watch-video, and motion-graphics skills, along with the writing-for-humans and unslop guidance.

The separate screen recording is visibly distorted, but the screen inside the Program recording is intact. I’ll use that as the screen source and the higher-resolution camera recording for the speaker. I’m comparing the audio tracks and transcribing the explanation before choosing the cut.

The strongest takeaway is: don’t give one AI agent untrusted input, private data, and permission to send information out. I’m building the short around that warning, then your email example: let the agent classify, let code prepare the draft, and keep human approval before sending.

The main audio track has a lower noise floor than the alternate track, and the camera stays aligned within about one frame across the take. The local DeepFilterNet pass also reduces pause noise without changing the duration. I’m now laying out the three-risk graphic and the email approval sequence, with captions kept above the platforms’ lower overlays.

The cut is now about 38 seconds. It opens with the temptation to connect an agent to every tool, explains the three risky permissions, and ends with the email approval workflow and your rule about keeping those permissions apart. I’m checking the layout at phone size before rendering the finished video.

The visual checks look good, including the longest two-line captions. I found two cuts close to speech sounds and am adjusting them against the waveform. Next I’ll check the encoded video’s loudness, sync, and full decode, then package the editable timeline and review page.

I kept the complete opening phrase so the short starts cleanly; the final duration is 39.6 seconds. The latest export is rendering now.
